essential_question: How can understanding portfolio, rehearsal, and exhibition help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Practice rehearsal plans with prompts, feedback, and gradually reduced support.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of rehearsal plans.
Check, revise, or improve work about rehearsal plans using stated success criteria.
lesson_success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about rehearsal plans.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.

materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool
task_brief: This is day 3 of "Portfolio, Rehearsal, and Exhibition". That is unit 6 in grade 5. Today is a guided practice (first pass) about rehearsal plans. It takes about 40–60 minutes. It is one day's work, not the whole unit project. Your unit is working toward this: Present a visual, musical, theatrical, dance, or mixed-media portfolio with process evidence. Today helps by working on rehearsal plans. Your unit also covers selecting work, artist statements, rehearsal plans, and peer feedback. Today adds real evidence toward your unit project.
primary_task: Make two small studies about rehearsal plans. You may look at the example while you work. After each one, write the choice you made. Write what you wanted it to do. Keep both studies even if you do not like them. They show your process. Then circle the one move you could not do without the example. You will test that next time. This work stays private unless you want to share it. Keep today's work tied to your unit. Today is about rehearsal plans. It is part of "Portfolio, Rehearsal, and Exhibition". Later days in this unit cover other things, like selecting work. Before you stop, do this check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about rehearsal plans; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. In grade 5, finish on your own. Write a reason for each main choice. If there were two ways to do it, say which one you picked and why.

guided_scaffold_note: Scaffolding for rehearsal plans fades within the session: the first case may be worked with the reference, model, or prompts in view, and the second must be attempted before checking anything. The supporting adult may ask "what supports that move?" after a step but should not supply the step. Where the unscaffolded attempt diverges from the scaffolded one, the divergence itself is the thing to examine, not something to erase.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: This task uses sound (rehearsal plans). You do not have to hear it to do it. You may use a written or drawn version, feel the beat by tapping or watching, or read the notes on paper instead.
You never have to perform in front of people. Showing one trusted grown-up, or just writing about it, counts the same.
You can take a break, stretch, or come back to this later. That does not lower your score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Provide a non-performance or low-audience option when needed without lowering the academic target.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting rehearsal plans.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for rehearsal plans follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for rehearsal plans, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for rehearsal plans works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of rehearsal plans, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking rehearsal plans mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply rehearsal plans under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on rehearsal plans rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
